import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
import io

# Data provided by the user
csv_data = """Person ID,Gender,Age,Occupation,Sleep Duration,Quality of Sleep,Physical Activity Level,Stress Level,BMI Category,Blood Pressure,Heart Rate,Daily Steps,Sleep Disorder
1,Male,27,Software Engineer,6.1,6,42,6,Overweight,126/83,77,4200,
2,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
3,Male,28,Doctor,6.2,6,60,8,Normal,125/80,75,10000,
4,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
5,Male,28,Sales Representative,5.9,4,30,8,Obese,140/90,85,3000,Sleep Apnea
"""

# Read the data into a pandas DataFrame
df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# --- Data Preprocessing ---
# Fill missing 'Sleep Disorder' values
df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None', inplace=True)

# Split 'Blood Pressure' into 'Systolic' and 'Diastolic' columns
df[['Systolic', 'Diastolic']] = df['Blood Pressure'].str.split('/', expand=True).astype(int)

# --- Visualization ---
# Set a modern and visually appealing style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", palette="viridis")

# Create a 2x2 figure for a comprehensive dashboard view
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(16, 14))
fig.suptitle('Comprehensive Health and Sleep Analysis', fontsize=20, weight='bold')

# --- Plot 1: Sleep Duration vs. Stress Level ---
sns.scatterplot(
    ax=axes[0, 0],
    data=df,
    x='Stress Level',
    y='Sleep Duration',
    hue='Occupation',
    size='Physical Activity Level',
    style='Sleep Disorder',
    sizes=(100, 400),
    palette='magma'
)
axes[0, 0].set_title('Sleep Duration vs. Stress Level', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[0, 0].set_xlabel('Stress Level (1-10)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].set_ylabel('Sleep Duration (hours)', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 0].legend(title='Metrics', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')

# --- Plot 2: Key Health Metrics by Occupation ---
# Melt the DataFrame to plot multiple metrics on the same bar chart
df_melted = df.melt(
    id_vars='Occupation',
    value_vars=['Heart Rate', 'Stress Level', 'Quality of Sleep'],
    var_name='Metric',
    value_name='Value'
)
sns.barplot(
    ax=axes[0, 1],
    data=df_melted,
    x='Occupation',
    y='Value',
    hue='Metric',
    palette='plasma'
)
axes[0, 1].set_title('Health Metrics by Occupation', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[0, 1].set_xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].set_ylabel('Metric Value', fontsize=12)
axes[0, 1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15)

# --- Plot 3: Blood Pressure Analysis ---
sns.scatterplot(
    ax=axes[1, 0],
    data=df,
    x='Systolic',
    y='Diastolic',
    hue='BMI Category',
    size='Age',
    sizes=(150, 300),
    palette='cividis',
    edgecolor='black',
    alpha=0.8
)
# Add reference lines for blood pressure categories
axes[1, 0].axvline(120, color='grey', linestyle='--', lw=1)
axes[1, 0].axhline(80, color='grey', linestyle='--', lw=1)
axes[1, 0].text(120.5, 76, 'Normal Systolic', color='grey', ha='left')
axes[1, 0].text(121, 80.5, 'Normal Diastolic', color='grey', ha='left')
axes[1, 0].set_title('Blood Pressure by BMI Category', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[1, 0].set_xlabel('Systolic Pressure (mmHg)', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 0].set_ylabel('Diastolic Pressure (mmHg)', fontsize=12)

# --- Plot 4: Daily Steps and Sleep Quality ---
ax4_twin = axes[1, 1].twinx() # Create a second y-axis
sns.barplot(
    ax=axes[1, 1],
    data=df,
    x='Occupation',
    y='Daily Steps',
    hue='Sleep Disorder',
    palette='inferno',
    alpha=0.7
)
sns.lineplot(
    ax=ax4_twin,
    data=df,
    x='Occupation',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    marker='o',
    color='dodgerblue',
    linewidth=3,
    label='Sleep Quality'
)
axes[1, 1].set_title('Daily Steps and Sleep Quality by Occupation', fontsize=14, weight='bold')
axes[1, 1].set_xlabel('Occupation', fontsize=12)
axes[1, 1].set_ylabel('Daily Steps', fontsize=12, color=sns.color_palette("inferno", 3)[1])
ax4_twin.set_ylabel('Quality of Sleep (1-10)', fontsize=12, color='dodgerblue')
axes[1, 1].tick_params(axis='x', rotation=15)
ax4_twin.set_ylim(0, 10)
# Manually create legends because of twin axes
handles1, labels1 = axes[1, 1].get_legend_handles_labels()
handles2, labels2 = ax4_twin.get_legend_handles_labels()
axes[1, 1].legend(handles1 + handles2, labels1 + labels2, title='Legend', loc='upper right')

# --- Final Adjustments ---
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.96]) # Adjust for suptitle
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
plt.close()
